desc: Derive transformation: middle distinct(i+1..j) = D(j) − cnt(values with last occurrence in [1..j] at position ≤ i); objective = Suf[j+1] + D(j) + f_j(i) where f_j(i) = P[i] − that cnt; range-add +1 on [p, j-1] when last occurrence of A[j] moves from p to j.
Implement the full Python solution (fast I/O, lazy segtree with range add / range max, main loop over j).

Verify correctness: trace through samples (expect 5 and 9), edge cases (N=3, all-equal → 3, all-distinct → N), and check indexing/off-by-one in segtree ranges and I/O handling. → Found real bug: first occurrences never establish the −1 subtraction on [j, n); old code gives 6 instead of 5 on Sample 1. Fix: always apply range_add(j, n, −1) when last occurrence moves to j (in addition to +1 on [p, j) when p > 0). Hand-traces with fix: Sample 1 → 5, all-equal N=3 → 3, all-distinct N=4 → 4.
Apply the bug fix to the code and stress-test corrected version vs O(N²) brute force on small random arrays plus both samples; deliver final corrected program.
